failure_modes.name: Query_Form_Mismatch
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 2 query: 'Is "All's Well That Ends Well," one of the three Shakespearean problem plays written between the late 1590s and early 17th century, chronologically earlier than the Rousillon Rupes scarp on Titania, which was first imaged by Voyager 2 in January 1986?' - This is a natural-language yes/no question rather than a keyword or entity-focused query suitable for passage retrieval.

failure_modes.name: Query_Stagnation
failure_modes.evidence: After hop 1 retrieved all necessary information (passages about Shakespearean problem plays, All's Well That Ends Well, and Rousillon Rupes imaged by Voyager 2 in 1986), the hop 2 query reformulates the entire claim as a question, and hop 3 returns largely duplicate documents (Rousillon Rupes appears 3 times, Shakespearean problem play 3 times, All's Well That Ends Well 2 times across hops 1-3). The queries fail to advance or seek new information.

failure_modes.name: Solver_Irrelevant_Passage_Overprocessing
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 1 solver reasoning extensively analyzes passages [3] (The Wild Goose Chase by John Fletcher), [5] (Whatever Happened to Old-Fashioned Love song), and [6] (Authorship of Titus Andronicus) which are clearly irrelevant to verifying the claim about problem plays and Rousillon Rupes. The solver notes 'Passages [3], [5], and [6] are not directly relevant' but still processes them at length.
